name: Al-Ma'ārij
meaning: The Ways of Ascent or The Ascending Stairways (Al-Ma'arij)
revelation_details: Makkan (Revealed during the middle Makkan period, a time when opponents openly mocked the warnings of Divine Judgment and demanded immediate punishment as a challenge)
core_theme: The absolute reality and inevitability of Divine Punishment, the cosmic scale of Resurrection Day, the psychological terror of sinners on Judgment Day, the inherent human weakness (Halū'a), and the character attributes of the honored believers (Al-Musallin).
name_origin:
The Surah derives its name, Al-Ma'arij, directly from its third verse:

• "From Allah, Owner of the Ways of Ascent (Dhi al-Ma'arij)."* (Verse 3)

Linguistic and Theological Significance

• Al-Ma'arij (The Ways of Ascent): Plural of Mi'raj, referring to the stairways, levels, or paths through which angels, spiritual decrees, and souls ascend into the divine realm across dimensions of space and time.
• The Sarcastic Challenge (Verses 1-2): The Surah opens by referencing a skeptic who demanded immediate punishment: "A questioner asked concerning a punishment bound to happen - to the disbelievers; of it there is no preventer."

Historical Context of Revelation

Classical commentators like Ibn Abbas (ra) noted that this opening was revealed regarding An-Nadr ibn al-Harith (or Abu Jahl), who arrogantly challenged the Prophet (pbuh) by saying: "O Allah, if this Qur'an is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment!" (as also referenced in Surah Al-Anfal 8:32).

The Cosmic Time Scale (Verse 4)

Allah emphasizes the transcendent nature of Divine authority and time:

• "The angels and the Spirit [Gabriel] ascend to Him in a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years."* (Verse 4)

Authentic Hadith Context: The 50,000-Year Day

The immense length of Judgment Day mentioned in Verse 4 is explicitly detailed in an authentic narration recorded in Sahih Muslim (Hadith 987a). Abu Hurayrah (ra) reported that the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said:

• "There is no owner of gold or silver who does not pay what is due upon it (Zakat), except that on the Day of Resurrection, plates of fire will be heated for him in the Fire of Hell, and his side, forehead, and back will be cauterized with them... on a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years, until judgment is completed between the servants, and he sees his path, either to Paradise or to Hell.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: The Impending Punishment, Cosmic Scale, and the Breakdown of Human Ties

points.label: The Skeptic's Demand
points.detail: A questioner mockingly demanded a punishment to fall upon the deniers.

points.label: The Absolute Inevitability
points.detail: Allah confirms that this punishment is coming upon the disbelievers, and no force in existence can avert or delay it.

points.label: The Scale of the Cosmic Day
points.detail: The angels and the Spirit [Gabriel] ascend to Him on a Day whose length and measure is equivalent to fifty thousand years of human time.

points.label: The Contrast of Perception
points.detail: Humans perceive Judgment Day as something distant or impossible (Yarawnahu ba'eedan), but Allah sees it as imminently near (Wa narahu qareeban).

points.label: Cosmic Upheaval
points.detail: On that Day, the sky will become like molten brass or dregs of oil, and the solid, towering mountains will be rendered like fluffs of carded wool floating in the air.

points.label: The Collapse of Social Ties
points.detail: No close, loyal friend will ask about their friend, even though they will be placed in full view of one another.

points.label: The Desperate Criminal's Ransom
points.detail: The guilty criminal (Al-Mujrim) will be so overwhelmed by the terror of the punishment that he will desperately wish to ransom himself from the torment of that Day using:

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
Surah Al-Ma'arij opens with a response to the mockery of disbelievers who demanded that divine punishment be brought upon them immediately, followed by a description of the cosmic reality of the Afterlife and the psychological horror of Judgment Day:
• The Skeptic's Demand: A questioner mockingly demanded a punishment to fall upon the deniers.
• The Absolute Inevitability: Allah confirms that this punishment is coming upon the disbelievers, and no force in existence can avert or delay it.
• The Lord of the Ways of Ascent (Dhul-Ma'arij): This decree originates from Allah, the Possessor of the high ways of ascent through which angels and spiritual realms ascend.
• The Scale of the Cosmic Day: The angels and the Spirit [Gabriel] ascend to Him on a Day whose length and measure is equivalent to fifty thousand years of human time.
• The Command for Beautiful Patience (Sabran Jameela): Allah commands the Prophet (pbuh) to practice "beautiful patience" - patience untainted by complaint, despair, or resentment.
• The Contrast of Perception: Humans perceive Judgment Day as something distant or impossible (Yarawnahu ba'eedan), but Allah sees it as imminently near (Wa narahu qareeban).
• Cosmic Upheaval: On that Day, the sky will become like molten brass or dregs of oil, and the solid, towering mountains will be rendered like fluffs of carded wool floating in the air.
• The Collapse of Social Ties: No close, loyal friend will ask about their friend, even though they will be placed in full view of one another.
• The Desperate Criminal's Ransom: The guilty criminal (Al-Mujrim) will be so overwhelmed by the terror of the punishment that he will desperately wish to ransom himself from the torment of that Day using:
• His own children,
• His wife,
• His brother,
• His closest family and tribe who sheltered and protected him in life,
• And everyone on the entire face of the earth combined, if only it could save him!
verse_breakdowns.reflection:
The opening of Surah Al-Ma'arij highlights a classic psychological trap: assuming that delayed judgment equals non-existent judgment. Skeptics often mistake Allah's patience for inaction. In response, Allah reveals the concept of Dhul-Ma'arij (Lord of the Ways of Ascent) and the cosmic scale of time - where a single Day equals 50,000 earthly years. What feels long to mortal, finite creatures is merely a brief moment in divine wisdom.
To survive the pressure of mockery and delays, the Prophet (pbuh) is instructed to adopt Sabran Jameela ("beautiful patience"). True patience is not passive resignation; it is maintaining inner dignity, trust, and emotional composure while waiting for divine justice.
The psychological climax of this passage occurs in verses 10-14. On Earth, human love is anchored in family - parents naturally sacrifice everything for their children, spouses, and kin. Yet, on the Day of Reckoning, the terror of judgment completely upends human instinct. The criminal is willing to throw his own children, spouse, family, and all of humanity into the Fire if it would buy him a single moment of safety. It staggers the mind to realize that the very people we compromise our ethics for today will become the currency we wish to throw into the fire tomorrow.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: The Blazing Fire, the Flaws of Human Psychology, and the Nine Traits of the Honored

points.label: The Rejection of Ransom
points.detail: Allah issues a stern refutation: "By no means!" No ransom will ever be accepted.

points.label: The Calling of the Arrogant
points.detail: Hellfire actively summons everyone who turned their back on the truth, fled from righteousness, and obsessively hoarded wealth without giving its proper due.

points.label: The Exception - The Honored Worshippers
points.detail: Excepted from this destructive human condition are those who perform prayer (Al-Musalloon) and possess nine foundational qualities:

points.label: Constancy in Prayer
points.detail: Those who are constant and regular in their prayers ('Ala salatihim da'imoon).

points.label: Economic Justice
points.detail: Those in whose wealth there is an acknowledged, calculated right (Haqqum ma'loom)...

points.label: Inclusivity in Charity
points.detail: ...designated for both the beggar who asks (As-Sa'il) and the poor person who is too proud to ask (Al-Mahroom).

points.label: Conviction in Judgment
points.detail: Those who affirm and truly believe in the reality of the Day of Recompense.

points.label: Reverent Fear of Judgment
points.detail: Those who are fearful of the punishment of their Lord - knowing that no one should ever feel arrogantly secure from the punishment of their Lord.

points.label: Sexual Purity and Integrity
points.detail: Those who guard their private parts, except with their legal spouses... while whoever seeks fulfillment beyond that are transgressors.

points.label: Trustworthiness
points.detail: Those who are scrupulously faithful to their trusts (Amanat) and covenants ('Ahd).

points.label: Upright Testimony
points.detail: Those who stand firm and honest in their testimonies, refusing to lie or hide the truth.

points.label: Guardianship of Prayer
points.detail: Those who strictly safeguard their prayers (Yuhafidhoon) - respecting its timings, focus, and requirements.

points.label: The Ultimate Destination
points.detail: These individuals will reside in Gardens of Paradise, honored and elevated (Mukramoon).

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
Allah refutes the criminal's hope for ransom, exposes the innate flaws of the ungrounded human psyche, and outlines nine character traits of believers who are saved from ruin:
• The Rejection of Ransom: Allah issues a stern refutation: "By no means!" No ransom will ever be accepted.
• The Nature of Hellfire (Ladha): It is a roaring, raging Flame (Ladha) that completely strips away the scalp and skin.
• The Calling of the Arrogant: Hellfire actively summons everyone who turned their back on the truth, fled from righteousness, and obsessively hoarded wealth without giving its proper due.
• The Diagnosis of Human Nature (Halu'a): Truly, human beings were created anxious, volatile, and impatient (Halu'a):
 1. When adversity or hardship touches him, he becomes fretful, despondent, and panic-stricken (Jazu'a).
 2. When good fortune or wealth touches him, he becomes stingy, withholding, and arrogant (Manu'a).
• The Exception - The Honored Worshippers: Excepted from this destructive human condition are those who perform prayer (Al-Musalloon) and possess nine foundational qualities:
 1. Constancy in Prayer: Those who are constant and regular in their prayers ('Ala salatihim da'imoon).
 2. Economic Justice: Those in whose wealth there is an acknowledged, calculated right (Haqqum ma'loom)...
 3. Inclusivity in Charity:...designated for both the beggar who asks (As-Sa'il) and the poor person who is too proud to ask (Al-Mahroom).
 4. Conviction in Judgment: Those who affirm and truly believe in the reality of the Day of Recompense.
 5. Reverent Fear of Judgment: Those who are fearful of the punishment of their Lord - knowing that no one should ever feel arrogantly secure from the punishment of their Lord.
 6. Sexual Purity and Integrity: Those who guard their private parts, except with their legal spouses... while whoever seeks fulfillment beyond that are transgressors.
 7. Trustworthiness: Those who are scrupulously faithful to their trusts (Amanat) and covenants ('Ahd).
 8. Upright Testimony: Those who stand firm and honest in their testimonies, refusing to lie or hide the truth.
 9. Guardianship of Prayer: Those who strictly safeguard their prayers (Yuhafidhoon) - respecting its timings, focus, and requirements.
• The Ultimate Destination: These individuals will reside in Gardens of Paradise, honored and elevated (Mukramoon).
verse_breakdowns.reflection:
Verses 19-21 present an unmatched psychological profile of unguided human nature (Halu'a). Without spiritual grounding, humans live in emotional extremes: a minor setback triggers total despair and anxiety (Jazu'a), while a taste of success triggers hoarding and selfishness (Manu'a). We are naturally fragile creatures driven by fear of loss and greed for gain.
The remedy to this emotional instability is provided in verses 22-34 through a comprehensive blueprint of 9 spiritual and moral habits. Notice that prayer acts as both the bookend and foundation of this list:
• It begins with constancy in prayer (Da'imoon - regularity),
• And ends with guarding prayer (Yuhafidhoon - quality, reverence, and timing).
Notice also how faith is intertwined with social responsibility. Believers do not view charity as a casual tip or optional favor; they recognize a "known right" (Haqqum ma'loom) in their wealth belonging to the needy. They do not only give to those who ask (As-Sa'il), but actively seek out those whose dignity keeps them silent (Al-Mahroom). By pairing deep worship with sexual purity, financial integrity, and truthfulness, believers transcend the chaotic weaknesses of human nature and earn the title of Mukramoon (the honored ones in Paradise).

verse_breakdowns.section_title: The Delusion of the Skeptics, the Oath of the Easts and Wests, and the Final Awakening

points.label: The Baffling Behavior of Deniers
points.detail: Allah asks Prophet Muhammad (pbuh): What is wrong with those who disbelieve, rushing toward you with necks outstretched, crowding around you from the right and from the left in separate groups?

points.label: The Unwarranted Entitlement
points.detail: Does every single one of them greedily hope to be admitted into a Garden of Delight (Jannatu Na'eem) without faith or moral effort?

points.label: The Reality of Human Origin
points.detail: Allah shuts down their arrogance: "No, indeed! We created them from what they already know!" [a humble drop of fluid].

points.label: The Oath of Divine Sovereignty
points.detail: Allah swears a solemn oath: "So I swear by the Lord of all the points of sunrise and sunset (Rabb il-Mashariqi wal-Magharib)...

points.label: Absolute Divine Power
points.detail: ...that We are surely capable of replacing them with people far better than them, and We can never be outdone or thwarted in Our plans.

points.label: Leaving Them to Their Delusions
points.detail: Allah commands the Prophet (pbuh): So leave them to sink in vain talk and play until they meet their promised Day!

points.label: The Emergence from the Graves
points.detail: On that Day, they will come out of their graves in rapid haste, as if they were racing toward a goalpost or an idol.

points.label: The Final Scene of Humiliation
points.detail: They will emerge with their eyes cast down in utter shame, covered in total disgrace and humiliation. Allah concludes: "That is the Day which they were repeatedly promised!

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
The Surah concludes by calling out the hypocritical eagerness of disbelievers to claim divine favors, swearing an absolute oath on divine power, and describing the ultimate humiliation of the Judgment:
• The Baffling Behavior of Deniers: Allah asks Prophet Muhammad (pbuh): What is wrong with those who disbelieve, rushing toward you with necks outstretched, crowding around you from the right and from the left in separate groups?
• The Unwarranted Entitlement: Does every single one of them greedily hope to be admitted into a Garden of Delight (Jannatu Na'eem) without faith or moral effort?
• The Reality of Human Origin: Allah shuts down their arrogance: "No, indeed! We created them from what they already know!" [a humble drop of fluid].
• The Oath of Divine Sovereignty: Allah swears a solemn oath: "So I swear by the Lord of all the points of sunrise and sunset (Rabb il-Mashariqi wal-Magharib)..."
• Absolute Divine Power: "...that We are surely capable of replacing them with people far better than them, and We can never be outdone or thwarted in Our plans."
• Leaving Them to Their Delusions: Allah commands the Prophet (pbuh): So leave them to sink in vain talk and play until they meet their promised Day!
• The Emergence from the Graves: On that Day, they will come out of their graves in rapid haste, as if they were racing toward a goalpost or an idol.
• The Final Scene of Humiliation: They will emerge with their eyes cast down in utter shame, covered in total disgrace and humiliation. Allah concludes: "That is the Day which they were repeatedly promised!
verse_breakdowns.reflection:
Verses 36-39 expose a subtle form of spiritual entitlement. The elites among the Makkan pagans used to sit around the Prophet (pbuh) in mocked curiosity, whispering in groups and arrogantly assuming that if an Afterlife did exist, they would naturally receive the highest status there just as they did in worldy life. Allah pierces their ego with a single reminder: "We created them from what they know." Remembering our humble biological origin is the ultimate antidote to spiritual pride.
In verses 40-41, Allah swears by His lordship over "all the points of sunrise and sunset" (Rabb il-Mashariqi wal-Magharib). Earth's position changes relative to the sun every single day, creating infinite horizons. The God who manages this vast, moving cosmic clock can easily replace an entire arrogant generation with people who love Him and honor His guidance. Human beings need God; God does not need human beings.
The Surah closes with a striking visual contrast: in this world, the disbelievers ran toward their idols and worldly desires with enthusiasm, while mocking divine warnings. On Judgment Day, they will be forced to run out of their graves in panic toward the ultimate Accounting, eyes lowered, covered in disgrace. The warnings they laughed at today will become the reality they cannot escape tomorrow.

deep_dives.title: Cosmic Upheaval and Psychological Terror (Verses 5-18)
deep_dives.content:
Allah commands the Prophet (pbuh) to respond to mockery with dignified endurance: "So be patient with gracious patience (Sabrun Jameel)" (Verse 5). Sabrun Jameel is defined as patience unmarred by public complaint or bitterness.

The Cosmic Collapse (Verses 8-10)

The Surah describes the physical atmospheric collapse during the Day of Judgment:

1. Sky Like Molten Copper: "On the Day the sky will be like molten brass/copper (Al-Muhl)." (Verse 8)
2. Mountains Like Tufts of Wool: "And the mountains will be like wool (Al-'Ihn)." (Verse 9)
3. Breakdown of Social Ties: "And no friend will ask [about] a friend." (Verse 10). Despite standing right next to each other, the terror of accountability leaves no room for social concern.

The Desperate Ransom (Verses 11-14)

Verses 11-14 present one of the most vivid psychological portraits of utter panic in all of scripture:

• "They will be shown each other. The criminal will wish that he could ransom himself from the punishment of that Day by his children, and his wife and his brother, and his nearest kindred who sheltered him, and whoever is on earth entirely, so then it could save him."*

Psychological Analysis

In worldly life, a human being instinctively sacrifices their own safety to protect their children, spouse, and family. On Judgment Day, however, the horror of Hellfire (Ladha) completely reverses human instinct - the sinner would gladly throw their own children, spouse, siblings, entire lineage, and all of humanity into the Fire if it meant securing their own release.

Description of Hellfire (Ladha) (Verses 15-18)

Allah firmly rejects the sinner's desperate hope for ransom:

• "No! Indeed, it is the Flame of Hell (Ladha), stripping away the scalp/skin (Nazza'atan lil-shawā). It calls him who turned his back and fled [from truth], and collected [wealth] and hoarded [it].

deep_dives.title: Human Nature vs. The Honored Believers (Verses 19-35)
deep_dives.content:
The Surah shifts to a profound psychological analysis of uncultivated human nature, followed by the specific spiritual discipline required to overcome it.

The Intrinsic Human Weakness (Verses 19-21)

• "Indeed, mankind was created anxious/impatient (Halū'a): when evil touches him, distressed (Jazu'a); and when good touches him, withholding (Manu'a)."*

• Halū'a: A composite psychological state characterized by extreme instability - lacking resilience during difficulty and lacking generosity during prosperity.
• The Cycle of Instability: When hit with hardship, the uncultivated human falls into despair and panic; when granted wealth or health, they become miserly, self-absorbed, and defensive.

The Character Checklist of Believers (Illal-Musallin) (Verses 22-35)

Allah makes a major exception: "Except those who perform prayer (Illal-Musallin)..." (Verse 22). The Surah details eight distinct moral and practical attributes that transform human weakness into spiritual nobility:

• 1. Constancy in Prayer ('Ala salatihim da'imun - Verse 23): Performing prayer regularly without abandoning it or treating it as optional.
• 2. Social Welfare Obligation (Fi amwalihim haqqun ma'lum - Verses 24-25): Allocating a recognized, fixed portion of wealth for the beggar (As-Sa'il) and the deprived (Al-Mahrum).
• 3. Belief in Judgment Day (Yusaddiquna bi-yawmi ad-deen - Verse 26): Living with active daily accountability, recognizing that actions carry eternal weight.
• 4. Healthy Fear of Divine Recompense (Mushfiquna min 'adhabi rabbihim - Verses 27-28): Avoiding spiritual self-complacency or false sense of immunity.
• 5. Sexual Chastity & Boundaries (Hafizuna li-furu jihim - Verses 29-31): Protecting sexual purity within lawful marital bounds.
• 6. Trustworthiness & Covenant Keeping (Li-amanatihim wa 'ahdihim ra'un - Verse 32): Honoring financial trusts, confidentialities, and social/contractual oaths.
• 7. Uprightness in Testimony (Bi-shahadatihim qa'imun - Verse 33): Standing firm for truth and justice in legal and social testimonies without bias.
• 8. Safeguard of Prayer Quality ('Ala salatihim yuhafizun - Verse 34): Protecting the proper times, inner focus (Khushu'), and conditions of prayer.

The Ultimate Destination (Verse 35)

The section closes by defining their eternal status: "Those will be in gardens, honored (Fi jannatin mukramun).

deep_dives.title: Refutation of Mockery and Final Vindication (Verses 36-44)
deep_dives.content:
The concluding section addresses the crowds of disbelievers who gathered around the Prophet (pbuh) to mock his teachings while arrogantly assuming they deserved Paradise if it existed.

Swarming in Mockery (Verses 36-37)

Allah describes their hostile demeanor: "So what is [the matter] with those who disbelieve, hastening before you, [sitting] on the right and on the left, in separate groups ('Izin)?" They swarmed the Prophet (pbuh) in satirical circles, rejecting his message while sarcastically asking if they too would enter the Gardens of Delight.

The Cosmic Oath and Divine Capability (Verses 40-41)

Allah issues a solemn oath by His divine power over orbital movements and cosmic realms:

• "So I swear by the Lord of all the risings and settings [of the sun/stars] (Rabb al-mashariqi wal-magharib), that We are indeed able to replace them with better than them; and We are not to be inhibited."*

The Final Horizon (Verses 42-44)

The Surah closes by telling the Prophet (pbuh) to leave the mockers to their vain talk until they meet their promised Day.

The Image of the Resurrection (Verses 43-44)

Allah describes the speed of their sudden emergence from death:

• "The Day they will come out from the graves rapidly as if they were racing to a goal post (Nusub) - their eyes humbled, humiliation covering them. That is the Day which they were promised."*

They used to rush (Mufti'in) to mock the Prophet (pbuh) in this life; on Judgment Day, they will be forced to rush out of their graves in terror toward an unavoidable Divine Recompense.
